Fitting and completing heights

Source: vignettes/fill-missing-heights.Rmd
fill-missing-heights.Rmd

fit_height() fits height by species, with optional plot adjustments. complete_heights() fills missing heights for subsequent stem calculations.

## Blank heights whose shipped origin is predicted
trees <- example_trees_pnw %>%
  mutate(ht = if_else(condition = ht_status == 'predicted',
                      true = NA_real_,
                      false = ht))

## Retain measured heights for fitting
measured <- trees %>%
  filter(ht_status == 'measured')

## Fit height with plot adjustments
fit <- fit_height(dbh = measured$dbh,
                  ht = measured$ht,
                  spcd = measured$spcd,
                  group = measured$plot)

The curves show population predictions against measured heights, separately by species.

Available forms are chapman_richards, curtis, wykoff, naslund, and schumacher. Species below min_n, or with unsuccessful separate fits, use the pooled relationship.

## Refill the blanked heights
completed <- trees %>%
  mutate(ht = complete_heights(dbh = dbh,
                               ht = ht,
                               spcd = spcd,
                               group = plot,
                               fit = fit))

## Compare refilled heights with the shipped values
comparison <- completed %>%
  mutate(shipped_ht = example_trees_pnw$ht,
         difference = ht - shipped_ht) %>%
  filter(ht_status == 'predicted')
tree_id refilled height (feet) shipped height (feet) difference (feet)
2 70.229 70.229 0
3 81.273 81.273 0

8 93.132 93.132 0

## Check agreement across every refilled height
comparison %>%
  summarize(maximum_difference_feet = max(abs(difference)))
#>   maximum_difference_feet
#> 1                       0

Predict heights

predict_height() predicts all supplied rows. Population predictions omit plot adjustments. Unseen groups use population predictions. Unseen species return missing heights.

## Predict heights and intervals for the small tree list
predictions <- predict_height(fit = fit,
                              dbh = example_trees$dbh,
                              spcd = example_trees$spcd,
                              re_form = 'population',
                              interval = TRUE,
                              seed = 7)
height (feet) lower (feet) upper (feet)

Intervals include group variation and residual error with fixed coefficients. They exclude coefficient and inventory sampling uncertainty.
